build.#: The zena command: the host binary and the CLI module it runs.

build:bundle.#: The zena command, with out/zena.wasm and the standard library embedded. Two scripts for one build: `build:bundle:cargo` declares no inputs, so wireit never calls it fresh and cargo is always consulted — cargo tracks its own inputs better than a `files` list could, and a no-op is a quarter of a second. This one names the binary cargo produced as an *input*, so its fingerprint changes exactly when the binary does, and that is what dependents inherit. `cascade: false` keeps `build:bundle:cargo`'s own fingerprint out: a script with no `files` is not `fullyTracked`, and wireit propagates that to everything downstream, where nothing can ever be fresh. Hashing the binary also makes freshness imply the binary exists, so a cache hit against an empty target dir cannot leave the scripts that run it failing with exit 127.

build:bundle:cargo.#: The one Rust build of the zena command. `--features bundled` makes the build script require out/stdlib_bundle.rs rather than fall back to a stub, so a binary that reports itself as bundled is one.

build:bundle-assets.#: Generates out/stdlib_bundle.rs from the standard library's sources and out/zena.wasm. bundle.zena is compiled and run on zena-run, which is what lets the zena command have one Rust build: the binary that embeds this bundle cannot also be the one that produces it.
build:bundle-assets.command: mkdir -p out && cd ../.. && ZENA_GC_RESERVE_MB=1536 ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. --dir packages/stdlib/zena::/stdlib packages/zena-compiler/zena/out/cli.wasm packages/zena-cli/dev/bundle.zena -o packages/zena-cli/out/bundle.wasm && ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. packages/zena-cli/out/bundle.wasm

build:module.#command: The compiler just built from source compiles the CLI module, run on zena-run with the preopens `zc` expects. It keeps its name section, like the compiler, so a trap in it names functions. Precompiling it is a separate script: it needs the zena command's binary, which is built from the bundle this module goes into.
build:module.command: mkdir -p out && cd ../.. && ZENA_GC_RESERVE_MB=1536 ZENA_DEBUG_NAMES=1 ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. --dir packages/stdlib/zena::/stdlib packages/zena-compiler/zena/out/cli.wasm packages/zena-cli/zena/main.zena -o packages/zena-cli/out/zena.wasm

test.#command: --release reuses the dependency artifacts the build step produced instead of compiling wasmtime a second time in the dev profile.

precompile:module.#: The CLI module's .cwasm, so the first zena commands do not race to run Cranelift on it. After the binary, because wasmtime's version is what decides whether a .cwasm can be loaded at all.
